claims.claim_text: Camber's auditor Marcum LLP issued a going-concern qualification; the Company has a working capital deficit of $0.9M and an accumulated deficit of $158.1M as of March 31, 2020, and states it will not have sufficient liquidity for the next twelve months unless the Viking Merger closes.
claims.source_quote: These factors raise substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern. ... The Company believes that it will not have sufficient liquidity to operate as a going concern for the next twelve months following the issuance of the financial statements included herein unless it can close the Viking Merger ... As of March 31, 2020, the Company had a working capital deficit of approximately $0.9 million ... Accumulated Deficit (158,074,768).
claims.subject: Camber Energy, Inc.

creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: SEC EDGAR submissions filter 8-K Item 3.01 (Notice of Delisting / Failure to Satisfy a Continued Listing Rule) for CIK 0001309082
creative_extensions.rationale: Going-concern + sub-$1 share price + repeated reverse splits is the canonical NYSE-American Section 1003 trajectory; an Item 3.01 8-K in the cutoff window would corroborate the distress claim.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: presence/absence of Item 3.01 8-K disclosures and dates
creative_extensions.signal_direction: presence corroborates distress; absence would WEAKEN (i.e. continuing-listing notices missing despite stated going-concern is contradiction-of-omission)

creative_extensions.source_label: PCAOB inspection / disciplinary database for Marcum LLP

creative_extensions.rationale: Marcum's small-cap reverse-merger audit practice has been a recurring PCAOB inspection target; pattern of going-concern qualifications across Marcum-audited microcaps would frame whether CEI's qualification is typical-late vs. typical-early.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: Marcum issuer-level inspection findings + comparable going-concern issuance rates
creative_extensions.signal_direction: CORROBORATES distress; not a contradiction test

claims.extraction_notes: H10 distress-cluster fingerprint: this claim is the anchor of multiple distress markers; supplemented by CEI-2 (reverse splits) and CEI-3 (toxic convertibles).

claims.claim_text: Camber executed three reverse stock splits in a 10-month window (1-for-25 effective Dec 24 2018; 1-for-25 effective July 8 2019; 1-for-50 effective Oct 29 2019), with the Oct 2019 split reducing share count from ~74.5M to ~1.5M; authorized common-stock count was then re-expanded from 5M to 25M effective April 16, 2020.
claims.source_quote: On December 20, 2018, the Company filed a Certificate of Change ... to affect another 1-for-25 reverse stock split ... On July 3, 2019, the Company filed a Certificate of Amendment ... to affect another 1-for-25 reverse stock split ... On October 28, 2019, the Company filed a Certificate of Change ... to affect a 1-for-50 reverse stock split ... reduce the number of common stock shares outstanding ... from approximately 74.5 million shares to approximately 1.5 million shares ... Effective on April 16, 2020 ... the Company filed a Certificate of Amendment to its Articles of Incorporation to increase its authorized shares of common stock to 25 million shares.
claims.subject: Camber Energy, Inc.

creative_extensions.rationale: Serial reverse splits at the cadence described are mechanically explained by listing-compliance triggers, not by share-price recovery; the pattern is a documented microcap death-spiral signature (Kerrisdale 'mind your t-bills' template).
creative_extensions.expected_observable: list of dated compliance letters timestamping each split
creative_extensions.signal_direction: presence corroborates death-spiral pattern; absence undermines the cadence interpretation

creative_extensions.source_label: Nevada Secretary of State business-entity filings (Certificate of Amendment / Certificate of Change)

creative_extensions.expected_observable: filing dates + amendment types matching the 10-K narrative
creative_extensions.signal_direction: CORROBORATES the chronology; absence/inconsistency would contradict

claims.extraction_notes: H10 cluster: 3 reverse splits in 10 months CLEARLY clears the >=2-3 markers within 6mo threshold and is a textbook microcap death-spiral fingerprint.

claims.claim_text: Between April 1, 2020 and June 24, 2020, Discover Growth Fund (holder of Series C Redeemable Convertible Preferred Stock) converted 498 shares of Series C Preferred into approximately 13,033,208 shares of common stock; the 2,951 outstanding shares of Series C still could convert into approximately 77,243,823 shares — versus only ~25M authorized shares.

As of June 24, 2020, the 2,951 outstanding shares of Series C Preferred Stock can convert, pursuant to their terms, into 77,243,823 shares of our common stock.
claims.subject: Discover Growth Fund / Discover (holder of Series C Preferred)

creative_extensions.rationale: Discover's conversion-and-sale cadence should leave a beneficial-ownership footprint via Schedule 13G amendments tracking its sliding stake under the 9.99% cap; absence of such filings while large conversions occur would be a disclosure gap.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: Schedule 13G/A or Form 4 filings dated April-July 2020 by Discover entities re Camber Energy
creative_extensions.signal_direction: presence corroborates the conversion narrative; absence raises a beneficial-ownership-reporting question

creative_extensions.source_label: EDGAR fulltext: prior CEI / Discover Series C agreements + S-3 / S-1 registration statements
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: edgar_fts on terms 'Discover Growth Fund' and 'Series C Preferred' restricted to CIK 0001309082, all forms

creative_extensions.expected_observable: prospectus filings registering resale of common shares issued upon Series C conversion
creative_extensions.signal_direction: CORROBORATES the dilution mechanic; missing S-1/S-3 registrations would be a separate compliance gap

creative_extensions.source_label: Toxic-convertible / 'death spiral' financier blacklist (Yorkville / GHS / Discover / Geneva Roth) cross-reference
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: EDGAR fulltext aggregate — count of distinct microcap issuers naming 'Discover Growth Fund' as Series C/D preferred counterparty over 2017-2021
creative_extensions.rationale: Cohort-level signal: if Discover Growth Fund appears as Series-C-style preferred holder across N other microcap issuers that went on to terminal-dilution outcomes, the pattern itself is high-signal for CEI.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: count of distinct CIKs naming 'Discover Growth Fund' as preferred holder
creative_extensions.signal_direction: high recurrence = high distress correlation; severity if Discover_partner_count >= 5

claims.extraction_notes: Classic toxic-convertible structure (reset/true-up conversion, no floor); ucc_proxy will pick up SEC Item 2.03 / 8-K disclosures of secured-debt / preferred-finance pacing. The 77.2M vs 25M authorized = unsustainable overhang.

claims.claim_text: Camber agreed to a merger with Viking Energy Group whereby Viking common-stock holders receive 80% of Camber's post-effective-time capitalization, contingent on closing by Sept 30, 2020 (extendable to Dec 31, 2020); Camber's near-term going-concern viability is explicitly conditioned on this merger closing.
claims.source_quote: each share of common stock of Viking issued and outstanding immediately prior to the effective time ... will be converted into the right to receive the pro rata share of 80% of Camber s post-effective time capitalization ... The Company believes that it will not have sufficient liquidity to operate as a going concern for the next twelve months following the issuance of the financial statements included herein unless it can close the Viking Merger.
claims.subject: Viking Energy Group, Inc.

creative_extensions.source_label: SEC EDGAR submissions API — Viking Energy Group's own filings (separate CIK)
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: edgar_fts and sec_filings.list_filings_by_form for Viking Energy Group's CIK; cross-check Viking's own going-concern + secured-note disclosures
creative_extensions.rationale: Viking is the merger target and the disclosed source of repayment for the $9.2M of Camber-to-Viking secured notes. Viking's own financial health + secured-note covenants determines whether the merger is mechanically realizable.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: Viking's 10-K/Q going-concern language; Viking's convertible-note holders' override consent status
creative_extensions.signal_direction: Viking distress = compound risk on Camber's only stated liquidity bridge; if Viking also discloses going concern, contradiction risk amplifies

creative_extensions.source_label: SEC EDGAR S-4 / proxy-statement filings for the CEI-Viking merger
creative_extensions.rationale: An 80%-of-post-merger-cap acquisition by a SEC-registered acquirer requires S-4 or merger-proxy; cadence + amendment trail tracks whether the deal is moving toward close or stalling.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: count of S-4/A amendments; gap between Form filings as a proxy for SEC-staff comment cycles
creative_extensions.signal_direction: extended amendment cycle = stalled; absence of an S-4 entirely = announced-but-not-actually-progressed merger

claims.extraction_notes: claim_evolution tests whether the Viking storyline persists / reaffirms in subsequent filings or whether terms deteriorate (e.g. multiple amendments, missed deadlines, restated exchange ratios — all of which preceded the 2021 close per Kerrisdale's later report; the framework should pick this cadence up via SILENT-or-AMENDED signals without us referencing post-cutoff news).

claims.claim_text: Camber produced 13,084 BOE total for fiscal year ended March 31, 2020 (5,399 Bbls crude oil + 18,892 Mcf natural gas + 190,503 gallons NGL) from 25 non-operated wells in Glasscock County, Texas — a 88% collapse from 113,685 BOE in FY2019.
claims.source_quote: The Company produced oil, natural gas and NGLs from 25 non-operated wells in Glasscock County, Texas during the year ended March 31, 2020 ... Crude oil (Bbls) 5,399 ... Natural gas (Mcf) 18,892 ... NGL (Gallons) 190,503 ... Total (barrels oil equivalent or Boe) 13,084 ... [FY2019] 113,685.
claims.subject: Camber Energy oil & gas production

proposed_connector.name: rrc_texas.query_operator_production
proposed_connector.description: Texas Railroad Commission Production Data Query — monthly per-operator per-lease oil/gas production
proposed_connector.sample_invocation: POST PDQ search by Operator Name='CAMBER ENERGY' + County='GLASSCOCK' + date range
proposed_connector.rationale: TRRC is the canonical regulator of every TX oil/gas well; the operator-level monthly production by lease is the definitive cross-check on the 13,084 BOE figure and the 25-well count. EPA FRS does NOT capture E&P production volume.
proposed_connector.completeness: all Texas wells with active permits

creative_extensions.source_label: Texas Railroad Commission (RRC) operator + lease lookup
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: https://webapps.rrc.texas.gov/PDQ/home.do — search Operator Name 'CAMBER ENERGY' or 'CE OPERATING' in Glasscock + Hutchinson Counties
creative_extensions.rationale: TRRC's PDQ system reports monthly oil/gas/NGL volumes by operator and lease; this is the authoritative production cross-check. Glasscock County 25 non-operated wells means CEI is NOT operator-of-record — operator-of-record lookup at TRRC tests whether the working-interest claim ties to real producing leases.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: list of leases naming CEI as working-interest holder; monthly production summing to ~13,084 BOE for FY2020
creative_extensions.signal_direction: if TRRC PDQ shows zero leases with CEI working interest, or production << claimed = contradiction; matching volumes within ~10% = corroboration

creative_extensions.source_label: Texas RRC Severance Order docket (Form W-3X / severance enforcement actions)
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: TRRC Public GIS Viewer + 'Severance' filing search by operator
creative_extensions.rationale: The 10-K explicitly references a May 30, 2019 TRRC Severance Order blocking sales from CEI's 11 Hutchinson County Panhandle wells; the existence + duration + scope of that severance order is a direct registry verification.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: severance-order docket entry with date 2019-05-30 + well-list
creative_extensions.signal_direction: presence corroborates the regulatory-enforcement narrative; absence = the claim is inflated

creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: EIA Texas production data + Glasscock County roll-up
creative_extensions.rationale: Cross-check whether a 88% YoY production collapse at a single small operator is consistent with county/basin trends or is operator-idiosyncratic; idiosyncratic collapse against a flat county baseline = operational failure signal beyond COVID alone.
creative_extensions.signal_direction: if county production is stable but CEI's drops 88%, the explanation is operator-specific, not COVID/macro

claims.extraction_notes: EPA emissions is a weak natural fit for E&P production volume (oil wells emit but TRI/GHGRP thresholds rarely fire at 25-well scale); PROPOSING rrc_texas.query_operator_production as the canonical missing source. Mapped epa_emissions as best-available catalog source for facility-existence cross-check only.

claims.claim_text: Camber sold 525 shares of Series C Preferred Stock to Discover for $5M in FY2020 and an additional 630 shares for $6M in June 2020; these proceeds funded a $5M and a $4.2M secured promissory note to Viking, accruing 10.5% interest, due February 3, 2022, secured by Viking's 70% ownership of Elysium and 100% of Ichor Energy Holdings, LLC.
claims.source_quote: On February 3, 2020, the Company and Discover entered into a Stock Purchase Agreement pursuant to which Discover purchased 525 shares of Series C Preferred Stock ... for $5 million ... On February 3, 2020, we advanced the $5.0 million raised from the sale of Series C Preferred Stock to Discover to Viking, and Viking provided us, among other things, a $5 million, 10.5% Secured Promissory Note ... On June 25, 2020, we advanced an additional $4.2 million to Viking in consideration for, among other things, an additional 10.5% Secured Promissory Note in the principal amount of $4.2 million.
claims.subject: Camber-Discover-Viking pass-through financing chain

creative_extensions.source_label: Viking Energy Group SEC filings cross-reference (Item 2.03 Creation of Direct Financial Obligation)
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: EDGAR submissions filter for Viking Energy Group CIK, forms 8-K, Item 2.03 entries between 2020-02-03 and 2020-06-25
creative_extensions.rationale: The $5M + $4.2M secured notes are mirror-image obligations on Viking's side; both should appear in Viking's own 8-K Item 2.03 disclosures with matching dates and principals, and Viking's secured-note disclosures should show the same Elysium/Ichor security interest.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: Viking's 8-K Item 2.03 filings dated 2020-02-03 and ~2020-06-25 naming Camber as lender + same security package
creative_extensions.signal_direction: matching = corroborates; missing or inconsistent terms = disclosure asymmetry / accounting issue

creative_extensions.source_label: TX/NV/OK state UCC-1 secured-debt registry (Elysium + Ichor pledge filings)
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: State UCC-1 lookup at Nevada SOS / TX SOS for debtor=Viking Energy Group / Elysium / Ichor; secured-party=Camber Energy
creative_extensions.rationale: A real $9.2M secured note backed by membership interests in Elysium + Ichor should be reflected in UCC-1 filings naming Camber as secured party; absence = the security interest is theoretical / unperfected.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: UCC-1 financing statement(s) naming Camber Energy as secured party
creative_extensions.signal_direction: presence corroborates perfected security; absence = security interest may be unperfected and the receivable less credit-worthy than stated

claims.extraction_notes: The pass-through structure (Discover -> CEI preferred -> CEI secured note to Viking) is the financial architecture that ties CEI's distress to Viking's distress; sec_filings.list_filings_by_form will count the 8-K cadence around these events as a distress-marker proxy.

creative_extensions.source_label: BLM oil & gas lease database + federal-mineral lease counterparty lookup
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: Bureau of Land Management AFMSS / LR2000 — federal oil-and-gas lease holder lookup by lessee name
creative_extensions.rationale: CEI's leases are explicitly described as TX (state and private mineral) not federal — BLM absence is EXPECTED and not informative as a contradiction; instead this confirms the company is NOT a federal-lease E&P which is consistent with the claim. Catalog usaspending presence test will fire as INFLATION_SUSPECT but should be interpreted as 'no claim made' rather than 'claim contradicted'.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: zero matching BLM leases for Camber Energy as lessee
creative_extensions.signal_direction: absence is EXPECTED (not a contradiction) for a non-federal-lease TX E&P

creative_extensions.source_label: SAM.gov UEI lookup by entity name (federal eligibility check)
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: sam_entity if a UEI can be resolved via usaspending output; declared primary NAICS and registration status
creative_extensions.rationale: Confirms the company's self-declared NAICS at the federal registry matches the filing's stated industry (oil & gas E&P, NAICS 2111xx). NAICS mismatch (e.g. SAM declares 541990 Other Professional Services) would be a strong scope contradiction.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: SAM primary NAICS = 211111 or 211112; registration status; CAGE code
creative_extensions.signal_direction: match corroborates; mismatch or no SAM registration is a real scope-claim signal

claims.extraction_notes: CEI does not claim federal customers, federal contracts, or federal grants — usaspending result will likely be INFLATION_SUSPECT but this should be interpreted as 'expected absence' (H5 over-fit guard) NOT as fraud signal. The query is run for completeness (entity-existence corroboration via UEI resolution) but the claim does NOT predict positive federal presence.
